newsitem.title: USA: Armey confident U.S. tax cuts can pass this year.
newsitem.headline: Armey confident U.S. tax cuts can pass this year.

text.p: House Majority Leader Dick Armey said Saturday Republicans were confident they could pass legislation cutting taxes before the end of this year and said a reduction in the capital gains tax remained a high priority.
"We expect the president to give up his insistence on higher taxes and to work with us, and we anticipate that he'll do that," the Texas Republican told CNN's "Evans & Novak" programme.

Armey, commenting on House Speaker Newt Gingrich's recent call for the repeal of the capital gains tax and the inheritance tax, said "total repeal and elimination of these two burdensome taxes" was unlikely this year.

"But we can certainly get a capital gains tax reduction; I expect to get that done," Armey said. He also said it was "not out of the range of possibility to eliminate death taxes," and that a reduction seemed possible.
He also said a child tax credit remained a high priority for Republicans.
Republicans are seeking tax cuts in this year's budget negotiations that are bigger than what President Bill Clinton has proposed.
